newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Zaire neighbors to stay out of fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Zaire neighbors to stay out of fighting.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it had urged Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi to stay out of fighting in eastern Zaire between Tutsi rebels and Zairean government forces.

"The United States appeals again to the neighbours of Zaire to stay out of Zaire, to not involve themselves in the fighting," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "We have underscored this message to Uganda and Rwanda and Burundi."

The rebels launched their revolt in October, accusing Zaire of denying them citizenship and seeking to return them to Rwanda, which their forebears left generations ago. An army counter-offensive has made little apparent headway.
"We're concerned about this situation and Secretary (Madeleine) Albright has taken the opportunity over the last 24 hours to transmit this message," Burns told a news briefing.

He said Albright had raised the issue at Washington meetings on Tuesday with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and on Wednesday with Foreign Minister Erick Derycke of Belgium, a former colonial power in the region.
Burns did not directly accuse Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of intervening in Zaire, but U.S. officials said there had been allegations of this.
